title: Asking for Permission: Can I, Could I, May I?

vocabulary.meaning_en: when someone allows you to do something
vocabulary.example: You need permission to leave early.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a polite act of asking for something
used to make a request more polite
vocabulary.example: Could I possibly borrow your pen?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who says good things about you to a new employer
vocabulary.example: Can I use your name as a reference?
It's a bit chilly in here.
I'm afraid that's out of the question.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the time by which something must be finished
vocabulary.example: We have a tight deadline today.
Can I have more pocket money?

fine_lines.title: Can I vs Could I vs May I
fine_lines.explanation_ar: Can I الأكثر شيوعًا وغير رسمية. Could I أكثر تهذيبًا. May I الأكثر رسمية وتهذيبًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Can I" is the most common and informal. "Could I" is more polite. "May I" is the most formal and polite.

examples.sentence: Can I have the last piece of cake, Mum?
Could I possibly borrow your phone?

fine_lines.title: "No, not at all" means YES
fine_lines.explanation_ar: عندما يسأل أحدهم Do you mind if...? (هل تمانع؟) فإن الجواب No, not at all يعني: لا أمانع، أي نعم تفضّل. انتبه ولا تفهمها رفضًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: When someone asks "Do you mind if...?", the answer "No, not at all" means "I don't mind", so it is a YES.

examples.sentence: Do you mind if I sit down?
No, not at all. Please make yourself comfortable.

fine_lines.title: Do you mind if I + present vs Would you mind if I + past
words: Do you mind if I open
Would you mind if I opened
fine_lines.explanation_ar: مع Do you mind if نستخدم المضارع، ومع Would you mind if نستخدم الماضي البسيط وتكون أكثر تهذيبًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Use the present after "Do you mind if I" and the past simple after "Would you mind if I" (more polite).

examples.word: Do you mind if I open
examples.sentence: Do you mind if I open the window?

examples.word: Would you mind if I opened
examples.sentence: Would you mind if I invited a friend for dinner?

expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to ask for permission.
expressions.example: Do you mind if I take off my coat?

expressions.phrase: Would you mind if I + past simple?
expressions.meaning_en: A very polite request for permission.
expressions.example: Would you mind if I invited a friend for dinner?

expressions.meaning_en: A formal, polite way to ask permission.
expressions.example: May I call you later if you're not busy?
Could I possibly borrow your pen?
Is it possible to move our meeting to another day?

expressions.meaning_en: Means "I don't mind" – a YES to "Do you mind...?"
expressions.example: Do you mind if I sit here? — No, not at all.

expressions.meaning_en: A formal way to give permission.
expressions.example: May I leave the room? — Yes, you may.
Could I use your phone? — Of course. Be my guest.

expressions.meaning_en: Tells someone to take what they want.
expressions.example: There's tea and water on the table. Please help yourself.

expressions.meaning_ar: خذ راحتك / اعتبر نفسك في بيتك.
expressions.example: Please sit down and make yourself at home.

expressions.meaning_en: Says someone can do something without asking.
expressions.example: If you're cold, feel free to turn up the heating.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to agree to help.
expressions.example: Can you help me? — It's my pleasure.

expressions.phrase: I'm sorry, that won't be possible.
expressions.example: Can we meet on Wednesday? — I'm sorry, that won't be possible.

expressions.phrase: I'm afraid that's out of the question.
expressions.meaning_ar: أخشى أن هذا غير وارد إطلاقًا.
expressions.example: Use the manager's parking space? I'm afraid that's out of the question.
Do you mind if I open the window? — I'd rather you didn't. It's cold.
Can I leave early today? — I'm afraid not. We have a deadline.

expressions.phrase: Yes, sure. / Go ahead. / Why not?
expressions.example: Can I have the last piece of cake? — Go ahead.
Do you mind if I come in late tomorrow? — Not a problem.
Can I go out before my homework? — Not a chance!

grammar.title: Modal verbs for permission: can, could, may
grammar.explanation_ar: نسأل الإذن بـ Can/Could/May + I + الفعل الأساسي. could وmay أكثر تهذيبًا من can. نضيف possibly لزيادة التهذيب: Could I possibly...?
grammar.explanation_en: Ask for permission with Can/Could/May + I + base verb. "Could" and "may" are more polite than "can". Add "possibly" to be extra polite: Could I possibly...?
examples: Could I possibly close the window?

grammar.title: Polite refusals instead of a simple "No"
grammar.explanation_ar: قول No وحدها قد يبدو وقحًا، خاصة في العمل. استخدم: I'm sorry, that won't be possible / I'm afraid not / I'd rather you didn't / I'm afraid that's out of the question.
grammar.explanation_en: A simple "No" can sound rude, especially at work. Use: I'm sorry, that won't be possible / I'm afraid not / I'd rather you didn't / That's out of the question.
examples: I'm sorry, that won't be possible today.

questions.question: "Do you mind if I sit here?" — "No, not at all." This means:
questions.explanation_ar: No, not at all تعني لا أمانع، أي يمكنك الجلوس.
questions.explanation_en: "No, not at all" means "I don't mind" – yes.

questions.question: Would you mind if I ___ a friend for dinner?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد Would you mind if I نستخدم الماضي البسيط.
questions.explanation_en: Use the past simple after "Would you mind if I".

questions.question: Which is a POLITE refusal?
choices: I'm sorry, that won't be possible.
questions.explanation_ar: I'm sorry, that won't be possible رفض مهذب.

questions.question: "I'm afraid that's out of the question" means:
questions.explanation_ar: out of the question = غير وارد إطلاقًا.

questions.question: "Do you mind if I open the window?" — You DON'T want it open. You say:
questions.explanation_ar: I'd rather you didn't رفض مهذب.
questions.explanation_en: "I'd rather you didn't" politely says no.

questions.question: "Not a chance!" is:
questions.explanation_ar: Not a chance رفض قوي وغير رسمي.
questions.explanation_en: It is a strong, informal no.

questions.question: A guest arrives. You want them to relax. You say:
questions.explanation_ar: Make yourself at home = اعتبر نفسك في بيتك.
questions.explanation_en: "Make yourself at home" tells a guest to relax.

questions.question: Is it possible ___ me to leave early today?
questions.explanation_ar: التركيب الصحيح: Is it possible for me to ... (هل من الممكن لي أن ...).
questions.explanation_en: Is it possible for me to ...
